summary: Ramp models struggle: a flat ~10% ramp needed to lift blocks would be ~10x longer than pyramid height (~1.5 km) with volume multiple times the pyramid; no archaeological remains of such a ramp at Giza; spiral ramps are slow single-file with ~20 corners.
content: To keep the lifting force low on a flat ramp, the ramp must be long, i.e., ~10 times the height it needs to reach... the final ramp must be ~10 times longer than the pyramid working height, thus ~1.5 km in its final state... No archeological remains of such a ramp have been found. ... spiral ramp models... are narrow and have corners... all spiral models include ~20 corners spiraling up the pyramid, where the blocks have to be rotated by 90°... single-file spiral ramp models are mostly standing, and it seems highly unlikely that single-file spiral ramp models could reach the pace to place 1 block every ~1 min.
